parts.note: Paris is the capital city of France
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital in Paris is run by a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the local congregation and district served by one church, a religious community.

definitions.meaning: sticks out or protrudes beyond a surface

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, juts out beyond something; as a noun, planned enterprises.

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds here change places

parts.note: a cane is a stick used for walking
to inscribe is to write, so inscribed means wrote

explanation.surface: A walking-stick is carved for someone's rainwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of CANE and WROTE to hear RAIN COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof, as a noun, is a coat that keeps the rain off.

clue.text: Fit southern university with computers etc

parts.note: IT, information technology, covers computers and related systems

explanation.surface: A southern university equipped with computers is a good match for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: To suit is to be fitting or appropriate for, as clothes fit a wearer.

indicators.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so the letters of the word before it are crushed and remixed

explanation.surface: Something alarming is happening at the very edge of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun (a field) but is the past participle of 'grind', signalling that ALARMING is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal describes something lying on the margin, the border or fringe of an area.

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor in amazement talks about some hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb meaning tamper with; it rearranges MENTIONS and HATS. 'in' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishment is great surprise or amazement, which is wonder.

clue.text: Reporter's way of walking in entrance

indicators.note: a reporter speaks out a story, so we want a word that sounds like the next one

parts.note: a gait is a manner of walking

explanation.surface: A journalist describes how someone walks in through the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reporter's' signals a homophone: GAIT sounds like the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is an opening in a wall or fence, a way in.

clue.text: Observe collection of books with pleasant covering

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: nice means pleasant
OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Watch a set of books being given a nice jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection of books' is the Old Testament, a standard crossword shorthand; 'covering' wraps the pleasant word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice is to see or become aware of something, to observe it.

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
asses are foolish people

explanation.surface: A student makes fools of some girls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasses is a northern British and Scottish word for young women.

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a rig is a set of apparatus or gear
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone tracks down where an oxygen apparatus kept in a house came from.
explanation.definitionFit: The origin of something is where it starts, its source or beginning.

clue.text: Tour oddly constrained by countries' laws

indicators.note: being constrained by something means being held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: states are nations or countries

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions, first and third, of the word beside it

explanation.surface: A diplomatic tour is oddly restricted by the legislation of various nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps the first and third letters of Tour; 'constrained by' sets them inside the word for countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written acts passed by a legislature, which are laws.

clue.text: Engineer designs a last ornamentation for church

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An engineer plans a final decorative feature for a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' is a verb here, rearranging DESIGNS, A and LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Coloured glass set in pictorial windows is a traditional decoration in churches.

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, which is cut off here

parts.note: a peach is a stone fruit

explanation.surface: Each piece of fruit has had its top cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having tip removed' takes the first letter P from PEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every both mean all members of a group taken one by one, as in 'each day'.

definitions.meaning: the singer and bassist who fronted the rock band The Police uses this one-word stage name
a confidence trick or undercover police operation to trap criminals

explanation.surface: A senior police officer runs an undercover operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' has a capital because it is the band The Police, whose frontman was Sting; the 's stands for 'is' joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The musician's stage name and the slang term for an undercover set-up to catch criminals.

indicators.note: taking means swallowing up another piece, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: an ace is someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: A top specialist takes a few minutes over the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' puts M inside ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Employing American in capital of Germany

indicators.note: capital means the first letter, a capital letter heading the word

explanation.surface: An American working in the capital of Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital of' looks for Berlin but gives only G, the first letter of Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Using and employing both mean putting something to use.

clue.text: Vessels initially brought over all the supplies

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The ships first brought across all the provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of brought, over, all, the, supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Boats are small ships or craft, which are vessels.

indicators.note: mistakenly means in error, so the letters that follow are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A kidnapper wrongly demands that the ransom message be put out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mistakenly' rearranges INSIST and RANSOM together; 'is' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A transmission is a programme sent out over radio or television, a broadcast.

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word, here the second and fourth

parts.note: a member is an elected representative, as a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Keep in mind the armed delegate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of armed, R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember is to keep something in mind and not let it slip.

clue.text: Flag set in position on a road

parts.note: to stand something is to set it upright in place

explanation.surface: A banner is put up beside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner or ensign carried as an emblem.

indicators.note: protects means holds safely inside, so the answer sits within the words before it

explanation.surface: A winter mitten keeps the hands warm only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' keeps the answer inside wINTER MITTEN Thermally.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotty in the sense of patchy or irregular means occurring at intervals, stopping and starting.

clue.text: Small drink supports energy for idle chatter

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so these pieces come below

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A little drink gives a boost of energy for some idle talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts S and SIP under GO in the down entry; 'for' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is casual talk about other people's affairs, idle chatter.

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a thespian is an actor

explanation.surface: Loudness is a trait of an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is an element or feature that contributes to something, a characteristic.

indicators.note: seen in means visible within, so the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A distinctive outline can be spotted in a Colorado valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' finds the answer across coloradO VALley.
explanation.definitionFit: An oval is an egg-like rounded outline, a geometric shape.

parts.note: a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: Some fellow is working as a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is someone employed to gather secret intelligence, a spy.

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of each word, here the middle two letters

explanation.surface: At heart, a wild goat needs only its basic diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes the middle two letters of ibex and of want: BE and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans are a basic, cheap source of protein eaten widely, a staple food.

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of each word it governs

parts.note: ID, identification, means identity papers

explanation.surface: A network is at last printing our newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letters of publishing and our, G and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of lines, or a power distribution network.

clue.text: Starts to generate amusement, laughter and festivity

indicators.note: starts to means the beginnings of each word, so take first letters

explanation.surface: Getting a party going creates fun and laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' takes the first letters of generate, amusement, laughter, and.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or celebration.

clue.text: Dancing at US yard for part of the weekend

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: People dancing in an American backyard at the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges AT, US and YARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturday is one of the two days, with Sunday, that make up the weekend.

clue.text: Brazilian dance losing a character from Greece

indicators.note: losing means dropping a part, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: the lambada is a fast partner dance from Brazil

explanation.surface: A Brazilian dance loses a performer who came from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes one A out of LAMBADA.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: State of bliss exists in show

indicators.note: in places the word before inside the word after

parts.note: to parade something is to show it off
is means exists, as in 'there is a God'

explanation.surface: Pure happiness can be found in a spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exists' is the plain verb 'is'; 'in' sets it inside the word for a show or procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is heaven or any place or state of perfect happiness.

clue.text: Consecrated area of land in outskirts of Sunderland

indicators.note: in places the piece before it inside the piece after
outskirts are the outer edges, so take the first and last letters of the word

parts.note: an acre is a unit of land area

explanation.surface: Holy ground lies on the edge of Sunderland, an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives S and D, the first and last letters of Sunderland, and 'in' puts ACRE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacred has been dedicated to God and treated as holy.
